regional_origin: Island-wide (Sri Lankan Muslim / Malay community origin)

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: room temperature; beaten lightly with a hand whisk only -- do not use an electric beater, which over-aerates and produces a sponge rather than a custard

ingredients.name: Kithul jaggery
ingredients.notes: grated or crumbled; dark brown sugar or palm sugar are acceptable substitutes, but kithul jaggery gives the authentic earthy, slightly fermented flavour

ingredients.name: Full-fat coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 1 tin; do not use light coconut milk

ingredients.name: Cardamom powder
ingredients.notes: freshly ground from pods is best; can use nutmeg alone or a combination

ingredients.name: Cloves
ingredients.notes: optional; ground finely along with the cardamom

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: just a pinch, to balance the sweetness

ingredients.name: Cashew nuts
ingredients.notes: scattered on top after steaming as garnish

steps.instruction: Grate or crumble the kithul jaggery. Combine with the coconut milk in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until the jaggery is completely dissolved. Remove from heat and cool until no longer hot to the touch -- adding a hot mixture to eggs will scramble them.

In a large bowl, lightly beat the eggs with a hand whisk for about 3-5 minutes until smooth and slightly frothy. Do not use an electric beater -- over-beating produces a sponge-like texture rather than the authentic custard with small honeycomb holes.

Gradually pour the cooled jaggery-coconut milk into the beaten eggs, whisking continuously. Add the cardamom, cloves (if using), cinnamon (if using), and salt. Whisk until fully combined and uniform in colour.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a steamer-safe mould or bowl. Do not fill to the brim; the mixture rises slightly during steaming.
Cover the mould tightly with aluminium foil. Place a thick cloth or tea towel over the steamer lid before closing -- this absorbs condensation and prevents water dripping into the watalappan.

Steam over medium-low heat for 40-50 minutes, until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Do not lift the lid during steaming. Check water level at the 25-minute mark and top up with boiling water if needed.

Remove from the steamer and cool to room temperature. Press cashew nuts gently onto the surface as garnish. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight -- the flavour improves significantly after chilling.
Serve chilled, scooped into individual bowls or turned out as a whole pudding. Traditionally served with sliced banana.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, loveandotherspices.com, serendipdelights.com, thebigsweettooth.com, cookingtheglobe.com, recipe52.com, dailylife.lk, and archanaskitchen.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 9+ independent sources; very strong agreement on kithul jaggery, full-fat coconut milk, hand whisking only, and cloth-covered lid technique
notes: Watalappan (also watalappam, vattalappam) is believed to have been brought to Sri Lanka by Malay soldiers during Dutch colonial rule (1640-1796) and remains closely associated with the Sri Lankan Muslim community, especially at Eid and weddings. Its key distinction from creme caramel is the deliberately porous, honeycomb-like interior -- small holes filled with syrup -- achieved by steaming at medium rather than gentle heat, and by not over-beating the eggs. Kithul jaggery is essential to authentic flavour; dark brown sugar is an acceptable substitute, but regular white sugar changes the character completely. Refrigerating overnight before serving is strongly recommended by multiple sources -- both flavour and texture improve significantly after chilling.
